name: @acorn/desktop
description: The desktop app: the Tauri shell, the Solid renderer it hosts, and the Node helper Rust supervises.

scripts.dev: pnpm run stage && ACORN_DEV_SERVER=http://localhost:4319 tauri dev --config src-tauri/tauri.dev.json
scripts.build: pnpm run stage && pnpm run build:renderer && pnpm run check:renderer-budget && pnpm run check:runtime-syntax
scripts.dist: pnpm run build && CI=true tauri build --config '{"build":{"beforeBuildCommand":""}}' && pnpm run verify:bundle
scripts.stage: pnpm run build:service && pnpm run build:bundled-plugins && pnpm run build:helper && pnpm run build:bridge && node scripts/stage.mjs
scripts.test: pnpm run stage && pnpm run build:renderer && vitest run && cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml

//build: The renderer is built here rather than by `beforeBuildCommand` so the startup-budget check runs against the bytes that get bundled and the bundler pass does not repeat a build that already happened; the inline config empties the hook for that one invocation. CI=true is what makes the DMG's Finder-cosmetics AppleScript get skipped — it needs Automation permission a build machine does not have, so the runner skips it either way and this keeps a local DMG the same shape as the shipped one.
//dependencies: The node's runtime dependencies. The staged service.js and the helper both resolve their externals from this package's node_modules, so they are declared here rather than in apps/node.
